notes: Strongest candidate so far: drivers/virt/fsl_hypervisor.c ioctl_memcpy — param.count is u64 from copy_from_user (FSL_HV_IOCTL_MEMCPY, requires /dev/fsl-hv access); num_pages = (param.count + lb_offset + PAGE_SIZE-1) >> PAGE_SHIFT stored in unsigned int (truncates 64->32), then kmalloc(num_pages * sizeof(struct fh_sg_list)=32 + 31) computed in 32-bit unsigned int; consuming loop for(i=1;i<num_pages;i++) writes sg_list[i].{source,target,size} into the undersized heap buffer. Need to verify product overflow conditions: num_pages must exceed 2^27/... to overflow the product (num_pages*32 as u32 wraps when num_pages > 2^27). count u64 -> num_pages = count>>12 (u32 truncation of 64-bit shift result). E.g. count = 0x100000000 (4GB) gives num_pages = 0x100000 -> product 0x2000000 (32MB) fine; count = 0x800000000000 -> num_pages low bits... (count>>12) truncated to u32; to get num_pages = 2^29 need count >= 2^41; product num_pages*32 = 2^34 wraps to 0 -> kmalloc(31) succeeds, loop writes 2^29*32 bytes -> heap overflow. Also num_pages itself is truncated from 64-bit shift, so kmalloc/pages sizes disagree with get_user_pages_fast count (num_pages int param too). Candidates classified below.
